Fit the initial hazard models

Source: R/fit-initial.R
fit_initial.Rd

Fits the initial (nuisance) hazard model for each event process (Cox models, or HAL), and the baseline treatment model if requested, and expands the data to the grid of all observed event times up to tau. It also builds the discrete product state space of the processes that other processes' hazards depend on. The result is the input to tmle_alpha(), calibrate_alpha() and calibration_curve().

Usage

fit_initial(
  data,
  fit_types,
  tau,
  treatment_model = NULL,
  a = NULL,
  max_count = 1,
  derived_vars = list(),
  depend_time = list(),
  prune_states = FALSE,
  use_exponential = FALSE,
  hal_control = list(),
  cores = 1,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame of observed event history data in long format, with one row per event and columns id, time and delta (the integer code of the process that jumped, with 0 reserved for censoring), plus any baseline covariates used in fit_types.

fit_types

A named list with one entry per event process, each either a model formula string or a list with elements:

  • model: a formula string of the form "Surv(tstart, tstop, delta == k) ~ covariates", where k is the process's delta code. Other processes can be used as covariates by name, in which case their counting process (lagged by one event) is used.

  • fit: "cox" (default) or "hal".

  • at_risk: an optional function of the data returning a logical vector, marking the rows at risk of the process (e.g. function(dt) dt[["z"]] == 0 for a process that can jump at most once).

Exactly one process must have delta code 0 (censoring).

tau

Positive number. Follow-up horizon; the target parameters are evaluated at tau.

treatment_model

Optional model for the baseline treatment A0, either a formula string such as "A0 ~ L0" or a list with elements model and fit (only "glm" is supported). Required when a is given.

a

Optional integer vector of baseline treatment values (0/1) to compute interventional hazards and clever weights for. Each value can then be passed as a to tmle_alpha().

max_count

Positive integer. Maximum number of jumps tracked per recurrent process in the state space.

derived_vars

Named list of functions of the data deriving additional state variables.

depend_time

Named list of functions describing dependence on the time since a jump of a process, keyed by process name.

prune_states

Logical. If TRUE, prune states not admissible under the at_risk functions of fit_types.

use_exponential

Logical. If TRUE, always transform the hazard increments dH to probabilities 1 - exp(-dH). Otherwise this is only done if some increments exceed 1.

hal_control

A named list of settings for processes fitted with fit = "hal", see Details.

cores

Positive integer. Number of cores used by parallel::mclapply() when predicting hazards across states.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, print model fits and progress.

Value

A list containing, among others, tmp.long (the expanded data with fitted hazards and clever weights), depend.matrix (the product state space), process.names, process.types, process.deltas, cens.process.id and at.risks.

Details

HAL fits are experimental and require a fit.hal() function to be available on the search path. hal_control may contain cut_time (35), cut_one_way (15), cut_tk (3), cut_tk_values (NULL), two_way (NULL), reduce_nk (0.025), sl (a list of HAL library specifications, built from cut_one_way, cut_tk, cut_tk_values and two_way by default), screen_two_way (FALSE), lambda_cvs, event_dependent_cv (FALSE), npenalize_vars (NULL), v_folds (10), seed (NULL), reduce_seed_dependence (FALSE), penalize_time (FALSE) and verbose (FALSE), with defaults in parentheses.

Examples

# Illness-death data: z is an illness that can occur once, outcome1 is
# death, and delta = 0 is censoring.
head(illness_death)
#>   id      time delta         L0
#> 1  1 1.0836890     1  0.2724785
#> 2  2 0.6539194     1  0.3572619
#> 3  3 0.1212156     1 -0.8616620
#> 4  4 1.1416233     2  0.8083350
#> 5  4 3.6778032     1  0.8083350
#> 6  5 1.0962284     2  0.6127352

fit <- fit_initial(
  illness_death,
  fit_types = list(
    z = list(
      model = "Surv(tstart, tstop, delta == 2) ~ L0",
      at_risk = function(dt) dt[["z"]] == 0
    ),
    outcome1 = "Surv(tstart, tstop, delta == 1) ~ L0 + z",
    censoring = "Surv(tstart, tstop, delta == 0) ~ L0"
  ),
  tau = 1
)
fit$process.types
#> $z
#> [1] "one.jump"
#> 
#> $outcome1
#> [1] "terminal"
#> 
#> $censoring
#> [1] "terminal"
#>
